t: You're standing on Houndsditch, a street running along the line of the old ditch that sat outside the London Wall, between Bishopsgate and Aldgate. The name may come from rubbish dumped in the ditch, including dead dogs, or from feral dogs scavenging there. Another idea is that the City hunt kept its kennels nearby. People born on this street include Jeremy Bentham, the philosopher and social reformer regarded as the founder of modern utilitarianism, and Joseph Nathan, a businessman who spent thirty years in New Zealand before coming back to London in 1887.
